headline: Tech sell-off deepens on AI-cost fears — but credit stays calm, a valuation correction, not a macro break.
stance: Nasdaq-100 futures are −1.2% pre-market as the AI-cost sell-off spreads overseas (Korea's Kospi −8%), yet credit, funding and bond volatility stay calm — this reads as a tech/valuation correction, not a credit event. The yen at 40-year lows is the wildcard, and today is quarter-end.

news.head: Global tech sell-off deepening
news.body: AI-infrastructure cost concerns are spreading; South Korea's Kospi fell 8% overnight.

news.head: US-Iran peace talks advancing
news.body: Oil eases as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds — WTI prior close $71.61, Brent $75.00.

news.head: Solid US data, Fed stays put
news.body: Q1 GDP revised higher and PCE came in line with expectations; rate-cut bets trimmed slightly.

implications: Credit is calm and liquidity ample — this looks like a tech/valuation correction, not a macro break; no need to panic-sell.
The yen at 40-year lows is the wildcard: BOJ action could spike currency volatility and force unwinding of positions funded by cheap-yen borrowing, rippling into risk assets.
Copper at 3-year highs alongside elevated gold is inconsistent with a growth scare — likely China-driven demand, not global acceleration.
Single name: AUGO (Aura Minerals, a gold & silver miner) — insiders buying plus large off-exchange block purchases; a way to play gold if haven demand persists.

watch.head: Nasdaq at the open
watch.body: another leg down shifts this from sector rotation to broad de-risking.

watch.head: USD/JPY above 162
watch.body: watch for any Bank of Japan commentary or intervention.

watch.head: US-Iran headlines
watch.body: further oil downside if talks keep progressing.

watch.head: Quarter-end rebalancing
watch.body: today is Q2 close — could amplify large-cap tech selling into the bell.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10Y Treasury 4.40% (prior close), edging lower overnight on mild safe-haven flows; 2Y at 4.09%, the curve +31bp — modestly positive for the first time since 2022.
Fed on hold: Q1 GDP revised higher, PCE in line; rate-cut bets trimmed slightly.
USD/JPY 161.8 overnight — the yen at its weakest since 1986; BOJ intervention risk is live. DXY 101.5, EUR/USD 1.138.
sections.positioning: Small-cap speculators have almost no bullish bets left — at a 3-year floor; a contrarian support level for the Russell 2000.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 futures −0.5% pre-market; prior close S&P 7,357 (flat), Nasdaq-100 −0.5%, Dow +0.1% at 51,921.
Nasdaq-100 futures −1.2% — tech selling deepening overnight; Korea's Kospi fell 8% on AI-infrastructure cost fears.
Thursday: Apple −6.1%, Microsoft −3.5%, Amazon −3.1%, Meta −2.7%, Nvidia −1.6%. Micron +15.7% on earnings, now −5% pre-market as the spike cools.
VIX 18.89 (moderate); Nasdaq volatility 30.91 — stress concentrated in tech. CAPE at 41 — stretched.

single_name.note: (Taiwan Semiconductor) — insiders buying, a burst of unusual options buying, and large off-exchange block purchases; a way to play a semiconductor recovery if the sell-off stabilizes.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Investment-grade spreads 75bp, high-yield premium 276bp — both calm; bond volatility 67.1 (low); financial conditions loose. A tech/valuation correction, not a credit event.
sections.positioning: Bond dealers are warehousing high-yield inventory at 3-year peak levels — limited capacity to absorb further client selling if risk appetite drops.
